idea: The design source for Artisign's own preview shell — the tool designing itself. Every token that has a counterpart in src/preview/style.css :root mirrors it by value AND by role name: the 19 colors (accent #2a3edb, canvas #e5e5e5, the grey text scale from text #1a1a1a down to text-faint #999), the six spacing steps xs4/sm6/md8/lg12/xl16/2xl24, radius.pill 999px and shadow.menu. Those can be compared line by line with the implementation, so a drift in either direction is visible rather than a matter of opinion. The typography scale and radius.sm/radius.md have no custom property behind them — they are design decisions, not a mirror, and should be read as such.

decisions.title: Tokens mirror the shipped stylesheet by value and by role name
decisions.body: Where a CSS custom property exists in src/preview/style.css, the token takes that property's role name and its exact value — never an appearance-based name, never a 'close enough' value re-derived by eye, and never an existing token whose name is convenient but whose value differs. Values with no custom property behind them (the 0.95rem rail icon, the 17px chip line-height) stay literal rather than inventing a token that implies a binding that does not exist. This is what makes the design checkable against the implementation instead of merely similar to it.

decisions.title: A component instance's own style is discarded — vary through variants
decisions.body: Writing <span class="$tag-chip" style="background: $color.accent"> does NOT tint that instance: the renderer emits the definition's root style and drops the instance's entirely. Confirmed by inspecting the rendered output, where the accent override was absent and only the definition's grey remained. Every visual difference between two instances therefore has to be a named variant. $tag-chip carries default / active / ref / badge for exactly this reason, and $btn carries default / confirm / confirm-disabled. The upside is that ad-hoc per-instance drift is impossible by construction; the cost is that a one-off tint needs a named variant and a reason to exist.

decisions.title: Component refs inside slot content are not resolved
decisions.body: A $component ref placed inside an instance's data-slot content survives into the output verbatim as class="$view-tab", unresolved, and the slot content's element ids are stripped as well — so such a node can be neither styled nor addressed by a flow or a comment. This ruled out the natural composition for the topbar (a tabs slot filled with $view-tab instances carrying their own flow targets). The topbar instead carries its tabs in the definition, with one variant per active tab, and the view-switching flows start from the sidebar's screen list, which are real, addressable nodes.

decisions.title: The filter field lives in the sidebar; the Board tab reports its result, it does not duplicate the input
decisions.body:
CHR-618/CHR-621: filter and pins are ephemeral per-project state in the daemon, one filter shared by the sidebar's screen list and the Board tab, and the Board shows filter matches ∪ pinned screens. Two ways to expose the shared filter on Board: (a) give the board toolbar its own input mirroring the sidebar's, or (b) keep the sidebar's existing field as the only input and have the board toolbar report the outcome. Chose (b). Reasoning: the sidebar's `screen-filter` input already exists and is exercised on every other tab; a second input box on the board would either drift from it or force a visibly-disabled duplicate. `$board-toolbar`'s `status` slot instead carries a plain-text summary. This means the Board tab keeps its sidebar expanded whenever the filter is non-empty and relevant — `board-view` renders the 280px expanded sidebar with its filter field for this reason. The other screens in this set keep the 36px collapsed rail since their point is the toolbar/canvas state, not the filter.

Also decided in this pass: the pinned/filter-match distinction reuses two existing pieces rather than a new component — `$pin-button`'s `pinned` variant (accent-filled) marks any pinned tile regardless of match, and `$board-tile`'s `outside-filter` variant (dashed accent border + a `$tag-chip` `badge`) labels a tile "pinned · outside filter" only when it is on the board solely because it is pinned. A tile that matches the filter needs no extra badge; a solid border communicates that on its own (`$board-tile` `default`).

Christian did not object to CTO review's other three recommendations, which are therefore also decided: the dashed-border-plus-badge treatment is the final pinned-outside-filter marker; the agent-presented banner stays visible until the human dismisses it; "Clear pins" requires no confirmation dialog.

decisions.title: Board zoom is a continuous 5%–200% slider on a viewport-shaped grid; low-zoom screens must be arithmetically honest (in mock terms); overview zoom hides the unpinned affordance
decisions.body:
Christian rejected the first CHR-621 pass for lacking a slider: a preset-only zoom group (Fit/50/100/200) cannot get far enough below 50% to make an overview of a large project (he named ~186 screens) usable. `$board-toolbar` now embeds `$zoom-slider` (−/+ step buttons, a 140px track, a live percentage readout), range **5%–200%**, linear. `Fit all` and `100%` are quick-jump buttons left of the slider; 50%/200% are not separate buttons any more now that the slider covers that range continuously.

SECOND CORRECTION: the first `board-view-zoomed-out` (42 tiles at 17% with "Fit all" active) still contradicted its own toolbar state — 42 tiles at 17% only fill a small corner of the canvas. Fixed by using Christian's actual project size (186 screens) and deriving the zoom from the resulting grid: with `$board-tile`'s native 180×150px footprint and the board's ~1356×764px usable canvas area, 186 tiles arrange as a 17×11 grid of 76×63px mini tiles — `76 ÷ 180 ≈ 42%`. `$board-toolbar`'s `fitall-edgesoff` variant and `$zoom-slider`'s `min` variant were updated in place to show 42%. This 42% is a mock-scale number — see the THIRD CORRECTION below for why the real number differs.

This also fixed the label-hiding threshold, previously a guessed "<20%": at 42% zoom, `typography.size-xs` (≈12.5px at 100%) scales to ≈5.2px, illegible, yet 42% sat inside the originally-declared 20–100% "truncated" band. Replaced the guess with a legibility-grounded threshold: labels hide entirely below ~60% (`8 ÷ 12.5 ≈ 64%`, the point the scaled font drops under a legible ~8px); 60–100% truncates with an ellipsis; 100%+ shows the full name.

THIRD CORRECTION (same day): once `board-view-zoomed-out` had 186 real tiles, the 181 unpinned `$pin-button` `default` markers turned into visual noise burying the 5 pinned ones — the only thing an overview zoom is actually for. Applied the same ~60% legibility threshold used for labels: below ~60% zoom, the unpinned pin affordance is not rendered at all (in the full app it becomes tile-hover-revealed instead, which a static screenshot cannot represent, so low-zoom reference screens simply omit it); the pinned (filled) marker always renders, at any zoom, since it conveys state a hover can't substitute for. `$board-tile`'s own `mini`-variant usage notes state this rule at the component level so it isn't re-litigated per screen.

FOURTH CORRECTION (implementation measurement, post-approval): two facts from the shipped/real implementation were folded back into this decision. (a) The board's tile grid is **viewport-shaped**, not a fixed layout: column/row count is computed from the current tile list and the board's actual surface area so Fit all makes best use of the viewport; recomputed on screen-list change, window resize, and project switch — never while the human is actively dragging the zoom slider. This design's screens still use a simplified fixed-size 180px mock tile in a fixed 1440×900 frame for illustration, not this real dynamic grid. (b) Real tiles are 390×844 (actual on-screen proportions), not this design's 180px mock — measured against Christian's real 186-screen project, the true fit-all scale came out to ~7.6%, well below this decision's original 10% floor, which would have clipped his own "show the whole project" requirement. The slider floor moved from 10% to 5% to leave headroom below the measured value. `board-view-zoomed-out`'s 42% remains in the design file as mock arithmetic — its own screen notes now say so explicitly and point back here; it is not the real number and was never meant to be, only a demonstration that a large project needs to go well below the old 50% preset floor.

Ctrl/Cmd+scroll-wheel over the canvas and pinch-to-zoom move the same slider value — not agent-settable, browser-local preference, same status as the edge toggle. Clicking `Fit all` computes whatever percentage fits every currently-shown tile (filter ∪ pins) into the viewport and sets the slider to that value once; it is not a sticky toggle.

Also in this pass: `$board-tile` was promoted (component, variants `default` / `outside-filter` / `mini`) once the tile card repeated a third time (`board-view`, `board-view-presented`, then 186× on `board-view-zoomed-out`) — see its own `usage` notes for the slot/variant breakdown and why `$pin-button` stays a sibling instance rather than a slot fill.

decisions.title: Follow mode: two new colors for read/write highlights, geometry stays inline, topbar-variant control is a design-file artefact, feed click exempt from pausing
decisions.body:
CHR-628/CHR-629 (ADR-005), APPROVED by Christian as designed. Three new tokens: `color.activity-read` (#0d9488, teal) and `color.activity-write` (#7c3aed, violet) for the two highlight kinds, plus `color.warning-subtle` (#fdf1e0) for the paused-toggle pill background. Read = solid 2px teal outline, appears immediately, fades 1.2s. Write = 2px DASHED violet outline plus a translucent `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)` wash, appears after the write's re-render or a 1s grace, fades 2.5s. Feed depth N=50. Both durations, N, and the token colors are approved, unchanged from the original proposal.

Inspect overlay and comment outlines, verified against shipped code (`artisign/src/preview/style.css` `#inspect-overlay`, `artisign/src/preview/comments.js:13-14`) rather than assumed: inspect overlay is accent blue, solid (`outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); background: rgba(42,62,219,0.06)`). Comment outlines are amber (`#d97706`) — the selected-target state is solid, but the comment-MARKER state is `outline: 2px dashed #d97706`, so dash pattern alone does not separate the write highlight from a dashed amber comment marker; the separation is hue plus the write highlight's translucent wash and (whole-screen case) its "Updated" badge, neither of which the pre-existing highlights carry. Under protanopia/deuteranopia (the common colorblind forms, blue-channel perception intact) violet's blue component should stay distinguishable from blue-absent amber even when hue-naming is unreliable; under full monochromacy the wash/badge are the only remaining cues — recorded honestly, not treated as fully solved.

The whole-screen write case (`write_html`, can't be localized to nodes) reuses the write violet at 3px around the whole screen frame plus a small "Updated" badge — chosen specifically to avoid reading as an error (no red, no exclamation glyph).

Geometry: highlights on the actual demo screens are inline token-styled positioning, not `$activity-highlight` component instances — that component is a fixed-size Design System reference only, because this project's components don't reliably accept per-instance width/height overrides and a highlight box has to match an arbitrary node's real bounding box. Same precedent as CHR-621's tile/pin geometry.

Follow toggle: the design file's `$topbar` `follow`/`follow-paused` variants are a DESIGN-FILE ARTEFACT, not the real implementation shape — confirmed by Christian: in the shipped app the follow toggle is ONE always-present topbar control (state-driven, not forked per tab), same as Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode already are. The two topbar variants exist here only because this project's components can't parameterize a slot-filled instance by external state, so two illustrative static variants were built to prove placement and both non-off appearances rather than one dynamic control.

CHANGED by Christian: clicking a feed entry does NOT pause follow, unlike every other human navigation (which still pauses per rule 1) and unlike an open comment/inspect mode (still pauses). A feed click is exempt because the human is still just watching the agent's own history, not designing something themselves — so the next navigating agent call pulls the view straight back to the agent's live target, no resume needed. Everything else in the pause/resume precedence (rule 2: Board presentation pauses; resume is always explicit, never automatic on condition-clear) is unchanged and approved.

A `component:`/`pattern:` navigation target highlights inside the Design System view's standalone render, same treatment — built as a new screen (`follow-highlight-definition`) rather than patching the shared `design-system-view` reference screen (a patch-then-revert happened during this work; verified unchanged via screenshot). A mockup target (no node ids) gets a transient column-level cue instead of a node box.

Feed: `$activity-entry` (variants `default`/`write`/`error`/`deleted`) and `$panel-tabs` (Elements/Activity header) let the feed live inside the existing right-side panel rather than adding a fifth 1440px-canvas column. Full interaction spec lives as tag notes on `chr-628`, not duplicated here.

decisions.title: CHR-905 chrome themes: light and dark are two parallel token groups bound at the screen root (no native mode concept)
decisions.body:
Direction C (icon-led compact) was approved by Christian and promoted into the system; the CHR-909 screens that apply it were APPROVED by Christian on 2026-10-23. It introduces light AND dark chrome colours, which the design tooling cannot express natively.

**Finding (architecture question, not settled here):** `tokens.json` is a plain nested map; every path holds exactly one string/number value, a `$ref` resolves to exactly one value, and neither `get_design_system` nor `set_tokens` has any mode/theme concept. We did not invent a tool or format extension.

**Convention used instead:** two parallel groups with identical member names — `chrome-light.*` (the default theme) and `chrome-dark.*` — 30 members each (bar, sidebar, canvas, raised, field, hover, active, border, border-strong, text, text-secondary, text-tertiary, accent, accent-subtle, primary, primary-text, focus-ring, scrim, tooltip, tooltip-text, ok, warning, warning-subtle, error, danger, activity-read, activity-write, edge, connector, shadow-float). Non-themed values are single shared groups: `spacing` (+2xs, pad, 3xl), `radius` (+xs 4px, menu 8px), `size` (control 28, control-sm 24, control-compact 26, row-menu 30, row-section 32, bar-sub 36, panel-header 40, bar-main 44, chip-h 16, icon 18 / icon-sm 16 / icon-xs 14, indicator 7), `typography` (+ui-base 13, ui-sm 12, ui-xs 11.5, ui-2xs 11, ui-chip 10.5, ui-title 16, weight-medium 500, family-code).

**How a theme is selected:** the screen ROOT declares one custom property per member — `--chrome-<member>: $chrome-light.<member>` (or `$chrome-dark.<member>`) — and every component and inline style uses `var(--chrome-<member>)`. So the components are theme-agnostic and a screen's theme is simply which group its root binds. Implementation maps one-to-one: `:root { --chrome-<member>: <chrome-light value> }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { --chrome-<member>: <chrome-dark value> }` (Setting System = `prefers-color-scheme`). Sizes, radii, spacing and type are referenced directly with `$size.*` / `$radius.*` / `$spacing.*` / `$typography.*`.

**Verified limits of the tool (why it looks like this):** a token ref IS accepted as the value of a custom property; `var(--x, $ref)` (a ref in the fallback) is rejected (`unknown_modifier`); refs inside a `<style>` element are not resolved. Consequence: components cannot carry a light fallback, so a component rendered standalone (design-system view / get_screenshot of a definition) shows no theme colours — review components through a screen (`app-shell`, `chrome-c-shell-dark`).

**Per-theme repetition is inherent:** light and dark screens are full copies that differ only in the root's 30 bindings; the `repeated_pattern` advisories between `chrome-c-*` screens are this duplication, not a missed promotion.

**Other notes:** (1) The old flat `color.*` / `shadow.menu` tokens stay untouched and keep serving the app-shell family of screens until the per-area rewrite; the new groups supersede them for the chrome only (so `tokens-mirror-shipped-css` stays true for the shipped stylesheet until the frontend ticket lands). (2) The user-screen stand-in (the phone frame on the canvas) keeps literal light values on purpose — user screens are never themed, and its inline values are the only intended drift warnings. (3) The mockup used Material Symbols FILL/GRAD variation axes (filled on-state icon, GRAD -25 in dark); the renderer's injected icon font is not guaranteed to be variable, so the screens show outlined icons for the on-state and rely on the tinted fill + accent colour. Frontend: check that the bundled woff2 is a variable font before depending on FILL/GRAD.

decisions.title: CHR-905 mapping: old preview :root variable → new token / custom property
decisions.body:
Source: `artisign/src/preview/style.css` `:root`. Frontend implements from this table. New custom properties are `--chrome-<member>` (themed, light/dark) and keep the existing `--space-*` / `--radius-*` families (themeless). `chrome-*` below means both `chrome-light.<m>` and `chrome-dark.<m>`.

| Old variable (value) | New token → custom property | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-surface` #fff | `chrome.sidebar` → `--chrome-sidebar` for side panels; `chrome.bar` → `--chrome-bar` for topbar, breadcrumb bar, list wells; `chrome.raised` → `--chrome-raised` for cards, menus, dialogs, comment cards | one old value became three roles: pick by role, not by value |
| `--color-surface-subtle` #fafafa | `chrome.field` → `--chrome-field` (inputs, chips, inspector card, wells) | page background = `--chrome-canvas` / panels `--chrome-sidebar` |
| `--color-surface-hover` #f0f0f0 | `chrome.hover` → `--chrome-hover` | selected/active row = new `chrome.active` → `--chrome-active` (neutral, not accent) |
| `--color-canvas` #e5e5e5 | `chrome.canvas` → `--chrome-canvas` | follows theme; user screens never themed |
| `--color-border` #e2e2e2 | `chrome.border` → `--chrome-border` | |
| `--color-border-strong` #d6d6d6 | `chrome.border-strong` → `--chrome-border-strong` | outlined secondary buttons, dashed chips |
| `--color-accent` #2a3edb | `chrome.accent` → `--chrome-accent` | hue changes to teal (#0f8a7e light / #3fc4b4 dark); accent is only for on-state toggles, tag hit chips, focus border — not row selection |
| `--color-accent-subtle` #eef1ff | `chrome.accent-subtle` → `--chrome-accent-subtle` | on-state fill (icon toggles), hit chips |
| `--color-warning` #d97706 | `chrome.warning` → `--chrome-warning` | dark #f59e0b |
| (no var; #fdf1e0 literal) warning-subtle | `chrome.warning-subtle` → `--chrome-warning-subtle` | paused follow pill; dark #3a2a12 |
| `--color-error` #b91c1c | `chrome.error` → `--chrome-error` | dark #f87171 |
| `--color-danger` #c0392b | `chrome.danger` → `--chrome-danger` | dark #ef6b5b |
| `--color-activity-read` #0d9488 | `chrome.activity-read` → `--chrome-activity-read` | dark #2dd4bf |
| `--color-activity-write` #7c3aed | `chrome.activity-write` → `--chrome-activity-write` | dark #a78bfa |
| `--color-edge` #9aa0c0 | `chrome.edge` → `--chrome-edge` | dark #6b7090 |
| `--color-text` #1a1a1a | `chrome.text` → `--chrome-text` | |
| `--color-text-secondary` #333 | `chrome.text` → `--chrome-text` | merged: the 6-step grey scale collapses to 3 |
| `--color-text-muted` #555 | `chrome.text-secondary` → `--chrome-text-secondary` | |
| `--color-text-tertiary` #777 | `chrome.text-tertiary` → `--chrome-text-tertiary` | |
| `--color-text-faded` #888 | `chrome.text-tertiary` → `--chrome-text-tertiary` | merged |
| `--color-text-label` #8a8a8a | `chrome.text-tertiary` → `--chrome-text-tertiary` | merged |
| `--color-text-faint` #999 | `chrome.text-tertiary` → `--chrome-text-tertiary` | merged |
| `--space-xs` … `--space-2xl` (4 6 8 12 16 24) | `spacing.xs … 2xl` → same names, unchanged | new steps: `--space-2xs` 2px, `--space-pad` 10px, `--space-3xl` 20px |
| `--radius-pill` 999px | `radius.pill` → `--radius-pill` | new: `--radius-xs` 4px (menu items, tooltip, list rows), `--radius-menu` 8px; controls use `--radius-sm` 6px, dialog `--radius-md` 10px |
| `--shadow-menu` | `chrome.shadow-float` → `--chrome-shadow-float` | themed (dark = hairline white ring + deeper shadow); used by menus AND dialogs |

Not in `:root` but in the design's `tokens.json`: `color.overlay` → `chrome.scrim` (`--chrome-scrim`, 0.32 light / 0.55 dark); `color.accent-tint` → `chrome.accent-subtle`; `color.connector` → `chrome.connector` (`--chrome-connector`; dark #4a4743). New with no old equivalent: `chrome.primary` / `chrome.primary-text` (near-black / inverted primary button), `chrome.focus-ring` (rgba teal, 0.35 / 0.4 — reserved for keyboard focus), `chrome.tooltip` / `chrome.tooltip-text`, `chrome.ok` (connection dot, follow dot), `size.*`, `typography.ui-*`. Dropped: none — every old variable has a target above.

Components carrying the new look: `chrome-icon-btn`, `chrome-btn`, `chrome-tab`, `chrome-pill`, `chrome-dropdown`, `chrome-menu-item`, `chrome-tooltip`, `chrome-panel-header`, `chrome-chip`, `chrome-field`, `chrome-section-header`, `chrome-element-row`, `chrome-list-row`; pattern `chrome-menu`. They coexist with the old `btn`, `tag-chip`, `topbar`, `panel-tabs`, `follow-toggle` (used by the app-shell family) until those screens are migrated per area.

decisions.title: CHR-905 keyboard shortcuts: browser-safe single keys, shown in tooltips, menus and one reference dialog
decisions.body:
CHR-905 (Christian, 2026-10-23): keyboard shortcuts are part of the chrome refresh. Browser-safe by construction.

**Rules.** (1) Only plain single keys, plus Shift for the zoom presets and Collapse-all. (2) Nothing fires while a text field, textarea, select or contenteditable has focus. (3) Nothing fires with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt held, so every browser and OS shortcut (open, new, find, reload, zoom, back/forward) stays untouched; we never bind Cmd/Ctrl+O, Cmd+N, Alt+arrows or F-keys. (4) While a menu or dialog is open only its own keys are active (Esc, Enter, arrows, and the menu letters). (5) Each shortcut is shown where its control is: tooltips on icon controls ("Flow mode  F"), right-aligned hints in menus, and one reference dialog opened with ?.

| Area | Action | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Modes | Flow mode | F |
| | Comment mode | C |
| | Inspect mode | I |
| | Status bar | S |
| | Follow on/off | W |
| | Resume follow (when paused) | R |
| Views | Screens | 1 |
| | Design System | 2 |
| | Board | 3 |
| Zoom (Screens) | Fit | Shift+1 |
| | 50% | Shift+5 |
| | 100% | Shift+0 |
| | 200% | Shift+2 |
| | Zoom in / out (also Board slider) | + / - |
| Board | Fit all | Shift+1 |
| | 100% | Shift+0 |
| | Edges on/off | E |
| | Clusters on/off | G |
| | Collapse all clusters | Shift+G |
| Panels | Screens panel | [ |
| | Context panel | \ |
| | Elements panel | ] |
| Project | Open project menu | P |
| | In the menu: Open project... | O |
| | In the menu: New project... | N |
| General | Focus screen filter | / |
| | Cycle theme System / Light / Dark | T |
| | Close menu or dialog, leave mode | Esc |
| | Confirm dialog | Enter |
| | Show this list | ? |

Replaces the old menu hints (Cmd+O, Shift+Cmd+N), which are browser-reserved. Shown in: app-shell (Flow tooltip), chrome-c-shell-menu (O / N, P), chrome-c-shell-zoom-menu (zoom presets), chrome-c-shell-shortcuts (full list). Tooltips for Comment (C), Inspect (I), Status bar (S), Theme (T) and Follow (W) follow the same pattern as the Flow tooltip.

**Decided by Christian (2026-10-23):**
- Tooltips are centered under their button (anchor wrapper: top:100%, left:50%, translateX(-50%), 4px gap). The implementation flips or shifts a tooltip that would leave the viewport or cover a neighbouring panel; chrome-c-shell-offline shows the flipped case (right-aligned under the Live chip at the right edge).
- Zoom presets stay Shift+1 (Fit), Shift+5 (50%), Shift+0 (100%), Shift+2 (200%).
- The inspect highlight stays blue (#2a3edb); it does not move to the teal chrome accent.

decisions.title: CHR-905 direction C rollout: offline chip, theme-independent highlights, selection rule, widths
decisions.body:
CHR-905 / CHR-909 details recorded while updating all screens to direction C. Status: APPROVED by Christian, 2026-10-23.

**Live chip, disconnected.** Connected = green dot + "Live" (title "Live reload: connected"). Disconnected = red dot (chrome-danger) + "Offline", with a tooltip "Live reload disconnected, retrying"; shown in chrome-c-shell-offline and available as topbar variant `offline`. The chip is informational, never a button.

**Highlights inside the user's frame stay theme-independent.** They are drawn on the user's screen, which is never themed, so they keep literal old tokens (not --chrome-*): activity read = teal 2px solid ($color.activity-read #0d9488), activity write = violet 2px dashed + wash ($color.activity-write #7c3aed), comment marker = amber dashed, compare diff = amber dashed ($color.warning #d97706). The inspect overlay stays BLUE (DECIDED by Christian) (#2a3edb, 2px solid, 6% wash): the new chrome accent is teal and would collide with the activity-read teal, so inspect keeps the old accent hue. Read-teal vs chrome-accent-teal is the one remaining near-collision; read highlights live inside the frame only, the chrome accent outside it.

**Selection vs accent.** Selected rows (screen tree, variant tree, folder list, Elements row) use the neutral `chrome-active` fill with primary text; accent (teal) is reserved for on-state toggles, matching-tag chips, focus border and links.

**Panel widths** follow the approved C shell: Screens 264px, Context 252px, Elements 280px, topbar 44px, panel header 40px, breadcrumb/compare bar 36px.

**Mapping addendum** (see chr905-preview-var-mapping): `$color.overlay` rgba scrims used by dim/overlay layers inside user screens (phone scrim) keep the old token; the dialog scrim and every chrome overlay use chrome-scrim. `alpha($color.X, a)` washes become `color-mix(in srgb, var(--chrome-X) a%, transparent)` where X is chrome (cluster frames) and stay `alpha()` on old tokens inside user frames.

**Components changed in place** (names kept so existing screens resolve): topbar (variants default, design-system, board, empty, follow, follow-paused, new: offline), follow-toggle, btn, tag-chip, panel-tabs, kind-icon (Material icons), plus restyled via token mapping: activity-entry, board-tile (thumbnails stay light), board-toolbar, cluster-header, edge-label, micro-thumb, new-folder-btn, new-folder-row, pin-button, quick-chip, variant-card, variant-crumb, zoom-slider. activity-highlight is untouched (user-frame highlight reference).

component_usage.topbar:
The 48px application header, on every screen. Variants select which view tab reads as active — default (Screens) / design-system / board — plus empty, which is the pre-project state: title and a dashed project picker only. The canvas controls (zoom group, status-bar toggle) appear only on the default variant, matching the shipped app, where they are hidden outside the Screens view. Flow mode is pushed right with margin-left: auto; the topbar's own gap and padding are $spacing.xl (16px) — binding them to $spacing.md instead is the easy mistake, and it visibly squashes the bar.

CHR-628/CHR-629: two more variants, `follow` and `follow-paused`, added for the follow-mode toggle — each is a full copy of the `default` (Screens-tab) layout with a `$follow-toggle` instance (`following` / `paused` respectively) embedded directly in the definition, positioned right before the Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode cluster (margin-left: auto moved onto the toggle instead of `tb-flow`). These are additive — `default`/`design-system`/`board`/`empty` are byte-for-byte unchanged, so no existing screen using this component regressed. A production implementation would more likely parameterize follow state as a prop than fork variants per state × tab, but this project's components don't support that composition (a `$follow-toggle` instance can't be a slot fill either, per `no-component-refs-inside-slots`) — two illustrative variants were enough to prove placement and both non-off states without multiplying every tab × every follow-state combination.
component_usage.tag-chip:
Neutral pill for a tag on a screen row, a design-system chip, or the 'project' badge in the folder browser — the shipped CSS makes .tag-chip and the badge pixel-identical, so one component covers both and no second badge style should be built. Single slot `label`. Variants: default (grey), active (accent fill, for the selected row's first tag), ref (monospace on surface, for a $token or $component reference), badge (accent-subtle). Wrap several in a flex row with gap $spacing.xs and margin-top $spacing.sm.

CHR-736 adds two variants for the variant tree: `match` (accent-tint fill, accent semibold text) marks the tag that satisfies the active tag filter and is promoted to the first chip slot; `more` (dashed outline, no fill) is the `+N` overflow chip after the first two tags, its label is the count (`+3`), hover lists all tags.
component_usage.btn: Dialog and empty-state action. default is the secondary/cancel treatment, confirm is the accent-filled primary, confirm-disabled is the same at 0.4 opacity for a form that is not yet satisfiable. Single slot `label`. Primary sits to the right of secondary in an actions row.
component_usage.quick-chip: Quick-access folder shortcut in the project dialogs (Home / Workspace / Desktop). The current variant marks the chip whose folder is being browsed. Single slot `label`.
component_usage.board-toolbar:
Board-tab-only bar between the topbar and the canvas, 40px, same chrome tokens as topbar. Revised in the CHR-621 approval round: the zoom control is now a continuous `$zoom-slider` (10%–200%) rather than a fixed Fit/50/100/200 preset row — Christian's explicit requirement was that overviewing a large project (~190 screens) needs zoom well below any fixed preset. `Fit all` and `100%` stay as quick-jump buttons to the left of the slider (a vertical divider separates the two groups); 50%/100%/200% presets are dropped as separate buttons now that the slider covers that whole range continuously — only "Fit all" (fits every currently-shown tile) and "100%" (native scale) are common enough destinations to deserve a one-tap shortcut. Whichever quick-jump button matches the slider's current exact value gets the active (accent) treatment; neither is active if the slider sits at a value neither button represents. Edges toggle and the two slots (`status`, `actions`) are unchanged from before this revision — see git history / decision `chr621-filter-lives-in-sidebar` for that part. Variants: `default` (100% quick-jump active, edges on) for the standard working view, `fitall-edgesoff` (Fit all quick-jump active, slider near its floor, edges off) for a fully zoomed-out overview, `zoomedin` (slider at its ceiling, neither quick-jump active since 200% isn't one of the two shortcuts) for inspecting one screen closely.

CHR-736 adds `clusters`: the `default` bar plus `Clusters: On` (toggle, accent when on) and `Collapse all` (button) right after `Edges`. Use it on every Board screen once a project has screen variants (see board-view-clusters-expanded / -collapsed).
component_usage.pin-button: Pin/unpin affordance, used in two places: fixed to a board tile's top-right corner, and inline at the end of a sidebar screen-list row. No slot — the icon is a static inline SVG map-pin glyph (`fill="currentColor"`, monochrome, 12px), not an emoji — the first version used an emoji pin glyph and CTO review flagged poor contrast on the accent fill plus inconsistent rendering across OSes; the SVG fixes both. `default` (grey outline, muted `currentColor` icon) is unpinned; `pinned` variant (accent fill, white `currentColor` icon) is pinned. The `pinned` variant doubles as the pinned marker itself — it stays visible on a tile regardless of whether that tile currently also matches the active filter, which is what makes a pinned-but-not-matching tile distinguishable from a plain filter match (which never carries this component in its filled state). Always render one instance per tile/row, in whichever state is correct (default or pinned) — an affordance that only appears on hover is not discoverable in a static design and untestable by screenshot; every tile and every visible sidebar row should show one, matching or not, pinned or not.
component_usage.zoom-slider: Continuous zoom control for the Board tab, embedded directly in `$board-toolbar` (not a slot fill — plain nested instance, resolves fine since it isn't inside another instance's `data-slot` content). −/+ step buttons flank a 140px track; the filled portion and thumb position communicate the current value, the `readout` slot holds the live percentage text. Range is **5%–200%**, linear: thumb position `= (value − 5) / 195 * 140px` from the track's left edge. 5% is the floor — CORRECTED from an initial 10% once implementation measured the real numbers: Christian's own requirement (CHR-621) was that Fit all must be able to show his whole ~186-screen project, and real tiles are 390×844 (not this design's 180px mock tiles), so the true fit-all scale on that project is ~7.6% — a 10% floor would have clipped it. Variants are illustrative fixed positions for the screens that need them, not a continuous range of variants: `default` (100%, thumb ~49% along the track), `min` (~15–20% in the mockup screens — see each screen's own notes for its actual illustrative value and remember the grid this design uses is a simplified fixed-size mock, not the viewport-shaped grid the real board uses), `max` (200%, thumb at the right end). A screen needing some other specific value should compute its own thumb/fill offsets with the same linear formula rather than approximate one of the three variants. Ctrl/Cmd+scroll-wheel and pinch-to-zoom on the canvas move this same value — this is a browser-local UI preference, not agent-settable, same as the rest of Board's zoom/edge state (see design-system decision `chr621-continuous-zoom-slider` and the `chr-621` tag notes for the full state model, including how the real board's grid is computed).
component_usage.board-tile:
Board-tab tile card, promoted from inline markup once the same card shape appeared a third time (four tiles on `board-view`, three on `board-view-presented`, 186 on `board-view-zoomed-out` — the second-occurrence rule was already overdue). Slot `name` (plain text) holds the screen name; only `default` and `outside-filter` render it. `default` is a plain matching-or-unpinned tile (solid border, 180px wide, 120px thumb). `outside-filter` is the pinned-but-not-matching treatment (dashed accent border + a `$tag-chip` `badge` reading "pinned · outside filter") — use it only for a tile that is on the board solely because it is pinned, never for a tile that also matches the active filter. `mini` is the zoomed-out/fit-all form: no slot, no border-dash/badge distinction, no box-shadow-worthy detail — just a bordered block sized to the honest scale factor for that screen's zoom (see the `chr621-continuous-zoom-slider` design-system decision for the arithmetic).

At `mini` scale, only ever place a `$pin-button` sibling on a tile that is actually pinned — do not render the unpinned (`default`) `$pin-button` at overview zoom. Below the same ~60% legibility threshold that hides tile-name labels, an unpinned pin affordance on every tile is pure visual noise that drowns the handful of pinned markers a human is actually scanning for; in the full-size app this affordance only appears on tile hover at low zoom (a static screenshot cannot show a hover state, so mini tiles here simply omit the unfilled marker rather than approximate hover). Pinned markers always render, at any zoom, since they carry information a hover can't substitute for.

The `$pin-button` marker is never nested inside this component (nesting a component ref inside another instance's slot fill does not resolve, per decision `no-component-refs-inside-slots`) — place `$pin-button` as a sibling of the `$board-tile` instance inside a shared `position: relative` wrapper div.

CHR-736 adds the variant-cluster forms (108x100, ~0.6 scale, thumb 72px, name line 28px, all with slot `name`): `cluster` = main screen inside a cluster (no kind icon), `cluster-state` / `cluster-overlay` / `cluster-step` = a variant tile with the matching `$kind-icon` before the name and a state or sheet-over-scrim thumbnail. Use them only inside an expanded cluster frame; collapsed clusters use the plain `default` tile plus a `$micro-thumb` row. Place the instance in a positioned wrapper div.
component_usage.follow-toggle: Per-browser preference toggle for follow mode (CHR-628/CHR-629), off by default. Three variants: `default` (off — grey outline, muted dot, label "Follow"), `following` (accent-filled, live accent dot, label "Following"), `paused` (`$color.warning`/`$color.warning-subtle` pill, label "Follow paused" plus a `Resume` action in accent text after a divider — clicking `Resume` re-arms follow and jumps to the latest target). Placed in the topbar's mode-button cluster, immediately before Flow mode / Comment mode / Inspect mode — see `$topbar`'s `follow`/`follow-paused` variants, which embed this component directly in their own definition (not via a slot fill — nesting a component inside another instance's slot content does not resolve in this project, per decision `no-component-refs-inside-slots`; composing it directly inside `topbar`'s own template, the same way `$board-toolbar` embeds `$zoom-slider`, works fine). No slot: state is expressed entirely through the variant, there's nothing per-instance to fill.
component_usage.activity-highlight: Canonical style recipe for the two follow-mode highlight kinds (CHR-628/CHR-629), documented here at a fixed illustrative size for Design System reference and standalone screenshot — screens needing a highlight over an arbitrary node's actual bounding box do NOT instantiate this component (per-node geometry is dynamic and this project's components don't reliably take per-instance width/height overrides); instead they apply the same tokens (`$color.activity-read`, `$color.activity-write`, `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)`) directly, inline, positioned to the node in question — the same precedent already used for board-tile pin markers and canvas tile geometry elsewhere in this project. `default` (read): solid 2px `$color.activity-read` (teal) outline, appears immediately on a targeted read call (`get_screenshot`, `inspect_node`, `get_node`, `get_screen`, `get_mockup`), fades after 1.2s. `write`: 2px DASHED `$color.activity-write` (violet) outline plus a translucent `alpha($color.activity-write, 0.08)` fill wash — appears only after the write's re-render lands, or after a 1s grace if no re-render is observed, and fades after 2.5s. `write-screen`: the coarse whole-screen case after `write_html` (which the daemon can't localize to specific nodes) — a thicker 3px dashed `$color.activity-write` border around the entire screen frame plus a small pill badge reading "Updated" at the top-right corner, same 2.5s duration. The badge is what keeps this from reading as an error state (no red, no "!" glyph, positive-toned label) — see `follow-active-feed` for it applied to a real screen frame. Shape (dashed vs. solid) plus hue keeps read/write distinct from each other and from the existing inspect overlay (accent blue, in the Elements panel) and comment outline (assumed `$color.warning` amber per convention, not otherwise specified in this project) even for colorblind users. Both colors were checked against a dark screen background — see `follow-highlight-dark`.
component_usage.activity-entry: One row of the follow-mode activity feed (CHR-628/CHR-629), three slots: `tool` (mono, the MCP tool name), `target` (small muted line, e.g. "screen · checkout-cart" or "project-wide" for a broad read with no single target), `time` (relative timestamp, right-aligned). `default` = a read call: small circular dot in `$color.activity-read`. `write` = a write call: small SQUARE dot (same color family as the node highlight, shape difference kept for colorblind users) in `$color.activity-write`. `error` = a failed call (`ok:false`): red left border, tinted background, a small ✕ badge instead of a plain dot, tool name tinted `$color.error` — deliberately NOT styled identically to a normal row so a scanning eye catches it without reading the text; `cursor: default` (not `pointer`) since it never navigates. `deleted` = a call whose target no longer exists: whole row at 0.5 opacity, target slot replaced by a fixed "target removed" caption (do not fill the `target` slot on this variant, it's ignored), `cursor: default`. Both `error` and `deleted` are inert by design — CHR-629 decided disabled-look over a tooltip or toast for "this entry does nothing when clicked," consistent with how a disabled state reads everywhere else in this design system.
component_usage.panel-tabs: Small two-tab header for a side panel that now needs to switch between two bodies without spending another 280px column — built for the right-side panel's Elements/Activity split (CHR-628/CHR-629). `default` = Elements active (accent underline), Activity idle. `activity` = Activity active, Elements idle. No slot: exactly two fixed tabs, not a generic tab-bar primitive — promote a new variant (or a slotted generalization) only if a third tab is ever needed elsewhere; don't stretch this one to fit an unrelated case.
component_usage.kind-icon: Glyph for a screen variant's kind (ADR-006, CHR-727/CHR-736): default = state (grey outlined page with content lines), `overlay` = accent outlined page with a filled foot (sheet, modal, popover), `step` = amber `↪` arrow (stage of a sequence). No slot. Use it directly as a screen child (sidebar rows, crumbs, popover rows, tile name lines); inside another component's definition it resolves, but NOT inside a slot fill (decision no-component-refs-inside-slots), so text-only slots cannot carry it. 9px wide, sits before the name with a $spacing.sm gap.
component_usage.variant-crumb: One crumb of the variant breadcrumb above the canvas (CHR-732). `default` = the root (main screen) with a home glyph, `overlay` = a non-current overlay ancestor with the overlay kind icon, `current-step` = the current node (accent border and fill, step icon). Slot `label` = screen name (`…suffix` form for variants). Every crumb ends in a disclosure caret that opens the children/siblings popover. Separate crumbs with a `›` in $color.border-strong. Only three variants exist because the drawn path needs no more: promote a `state` / `current-overlay` variant when a screen needs it instead of restyling an instance (instance styles are discarded).
component_usage.cluster-header: Header line of a board cluster frame (CHR-733), 32px, sits at the top of the frame div. `default` = collapsed: chevron, main-screen name, muted meta ("· 9 · depth 2"). `expanded` = open: chevron down and an accent `▴ collapse` action pushed right; the frame itself carries the accent border (the component does not draw the frame, the wrapper div does). Slots: `name`, `meta`, and `action` (expanded only). Wrap the instance in the frame div and give the frame `border: 1.5px solid $color.edge` (collapsed) or `$color.accent` (expanded).
component_usage.micro-thumb: 12x26 micro thumbnail in a collapsed board cluster (CHR-733), one per variant, in a nowrap row under the main tile. `default` = state variant (grey), `overlay` = overlay variant (accent foot), `deeper` = a variant below depth 1 (dashed outline, 6px extra left margin). Cap the row at 9 and append a muted `+N` text for the rest. No slot.
component_usage.edge-label: Label pill on a board flow edge that docks on a cluster frame (CHR-733). `default` = the edge's TARGET variant (accent, dashed border, starts with `→`); `source` = the edge starts at that variant (grey, solid border, ends with `↦`). Slot `label` = variant name. Position it in an absolutely placed wrapper next to the dock point; the component has no positioning.
component_usage.variant-card: Titled card for the inspector's Elements tab (CHR-732): `Variant` (Path, Kind, Depth, Siblings, Flows in / out) and `Also reached from`. Slots: `title` (rendered uppercase, small) and `body` (fill with one wrapper element whose children are the rows; label left, value right via `display: flex; justify-content: space-between`). Rows are text only, since components do not resolve inside slots. Stack cards with a $spacing.lg gap inside a $spacing.lg padded wrapper above the element list.
component_usage.new-folder-btn: CHR-831. "+ New folder" button in the path row of the Open/New project dialogs, right of the breadcrumbs. `default` = idle, `active` = the inline new-folder row is open. No slot; fixed label.
component_usage.new-folder-row: CHR-831. Inline row pinned at the top of the folder list while a folder is being created. Slot `value` = the typed name. `default` = typing (accent input border, Create enabled). `error` = red input border, Create dimmed, extra slot `message` = the error text (exists / invalid / permission). Slot fills are text only.
component_usage.chrome-icon-btn: CHR-905 icon button, 28px (24px `sm`), radius 6, 18px (16px sm) Material icon in slot `icon` (ligature name as text). Variants: default (rest), `hover`, `active` (= on-state: accent-subtle fill + accent icon, used for mode toggles Flow/Comment/Inspect), `sm`, `sm-hover` (panel collapse, dialog close, variant-map). Every icon toggle needs a tooltip with label + shortcut, centered under the button: wrap the button in `position:relative;display:inline-flex` and put a `chrome-tooltip` in an absolute wrapper (`top:100%;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);margin-top:4px`). Near the right panel the implementation flips or shifts the tooltip. Shown once, on Flow mode in `app-shell` and `-dark`; the same pattern applies to Comment (C), Inspect (I), Status bar (S) and Theme (T). Never use for a stateful setting whose value must be readable (use chrome-dropdown). Colours come from `--chrome-*` custom properties bound at the screen root.
component_usage.chrome-btn: CHR-905 text button, 28px, radius 6, 13px, single slot `label` (fill with a `display:inline-flex;gap:6px` span when an icon precedes the text). Variants: `default` = secondary (outlined on raised), `secondary-hover`, `secondary-compact` (26px, dialog quick-access chips), `primary` (filled near-black light / inverted dark, medium weight; at most ONE per view, right end of an action row), `primary-hover`, `ghost`, `ghost-hover`, `ghost-on` (toggle on: active fill, e.g. Tags), `ghost-sm` (24px, 12px text, inline actions such as Reply/Resolve). Destructive is not designed yet (no screen needs it); add a variant using `chrome-danger` when one does. Use `chrome-icon-btn` for icon-only buttons.
component_usage.chrome-tab: CHR-905 underline tab, slot `label`. `default` idle (secondary text), `active` (primary text + 2px underline in `chrome-text`). Place instances in a flex wrapper with `align-items:stretch;align-self:stretch` inside a bar so the underline lands on the bar's bottom border (the tab has margin-bottom:-1px). Used for the topbar view tabs (Screens / Design System / Board) and, inside `chrome-panel-header` `tabs`, Elements / Activity. Not a generic segmented control.
component_usage.chrome-pill: CHR-905 pill toggle for follow mode (replaces the look of `follow-toggle`), slot `label`. `default` = off (tertiary dot, no fill), `following` (active fill + green `chrome-ok` dot), `paused` (warning-subtle fill, warning text and dot; follow with a ghost Resume button next to it). One always-present control, state-driven, not forked per tab (see decision chr629-follow-mode-highlight-language).
component_usage.chrome-dropdown: CHR-905 dropdown trigger: current value in slot `label` plus a 16px expand_more chevron. Variants `default`, `hover`, `open` (active fill while its menu is open). Used for the project picker (label = folder icon + name) and the zoom control ("Fit"). The trigger always shows the current value (anti-pattern: hiding a stateful setting behind an icon). The menu itself is the `chrome-menu` pattern.
component_usage.chrome-menu-item: CHR-905 menu row, 30px, radius 4, 16px check column, slots `label` and `hint` (right-aligned shortcut or path, 11px tertiary). Variants: `default`, `hover`, `checked` (current choice), `checked-hover`, `action` (18px icon in slot `icon` instead of the check column; for Open project / New project). Compose inside the `chrome-menu` pattern wrapper; dividers and section labels are plain markup there.
component_usage.chrome-tooltip: CHR-905 tooltip: inverted surface (`chrome-tooltip` / `chrome-tooltip-text`), radius 4, 11.5px, slots `label` and `key` (shortcut in a small kbd box). Variant `plain` = label only. The component has no positioning: wrap it in an absolute wrapper anchored to its trigger and CENTERED under it (`top:100%;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);margin-top:4px`), decided by Christian. The implementation flips or shifts it at viewport edges so it never covers a neighbouring panel header; the offline chip screen shows the flipped (right-aligned) case. Required on every icon-only control (label + shortcut).
component_usage.chrome-panel-header: CHR-905 side-panel header, 40px, bottom hairline, medium 13px title (slot `title`) and a 24px collapse icon button (it embeds `chrome-icon-btn` sm). Variants: `default` (collapse toward the left, icon left_panel_close: Screens, Context), `right` (right_panel_close), `tabs` (Elements active / Activity underline tabs + right collapse; no title slot), `tabs-activity`. The collapse control is always visible in the header; a collapsed panel becomes a rail (not designed here).
component_usage.chrome-chip: CHR-905 tag/info chip, 16px, pill, 10.5px, slot `label`. `default`; `on-selected` (raised fill, only on a selected row); `hit` (accent-subtle + accent, the tag that matches the active filter); `more` (dashed, the +N overflow chip); `ref` (monospace, node id in a comment); `token` / `token-hit` (18px monospace design-system reference in the inspector card). Also used for the variant kind label (overlay / step). Replaces the look of `tag-chip` for the new chrome.
component_usage.chrome-field: CHR-905 text field, 28px, radius 6, `chrome-field` fill with a hairline border, slot `value` (fill with the typed text). Variants `default`, `search` (16px search icon in front; filter in the Screens panel), `focus` (accent border; the focus ring token `chrome-focus-ring` is reserved for keyboard focus and not drawn yet). Grows with `flex:1`; place it in a flex row or wrap it in a block when it must not stretch vertically.
component_usage.chrome-section-header: CHR-905 section header inside a side panel, 32px, medium 13px. `default` = collapsible (chevron, slot `title`, slot `meta` right, e.g. the screen name for Notes); `with-add` = top and bottom hairline, no chevron, trailing 24px icon button (Comments + add_comment). Slots `title` and `meta`.
component_usage.chrome-element-row: CHR-905 Elements-panel row, 30px, monospace 11.5px, slot `label` (e.g. `<button> · btn-checkout`). `default` = collapsed (chevron right), `open` = expanded/selected (active fill, chevron down, medium weight); the inspector card follows the open row as plain markup.
component_usage.chrome-list-row: CHR-905 folder row of the Open/New project dialogs, 28px, 18px folder icon, slot `label`. Variants: `default`, `selected` (active fill), `project` (trailing "project" badge for folders already containing a project), `selected-project`.

pattern_usage.chrome-menu: CHR-905 menu / popover container (project menu, later the settings menu). A pattern, not a component, because menu items are `chrome-menu-item` instances and component refs do not resolve inside slot fills. Floating surface: `chrome-raised` fill, radius.menu 8px, `chrome-shadow-float` (hairline ring + soft shadow, ring flips to translucent white in dark), 4px padding. Section labels 11px tertiary; 1px dividers with 4px margin; no section header chrome. Position absolutely under its trigger; the trigger shows the `open` variant. Needs a screen root that binds the `--chrome-*` custom properties (see decision chr905-chrome-themes-parallel-token-groups).
